LESSON: WRITING 7.4.1 SPELLING

Grade: SNE  /  hearing-impairment / Grade two
Subject: ENGLISH LANGUAGE ACTIVITIES
Strand: Strand 7
Topic 7.4: Writing 7.4.1 Spelling
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 2

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Writing 7.4.1 Spelling, part of Strand 7 in SNE  /  hearing-impairment / Grade two ENGLISH LANGUAGE ACTIVITIES.

Key inquiry question: Why should people spell words correctly? 2. How do we learn to spell?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

Follow your teacher’s guidance for group work, discussion, and practice on this topic.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Writing 7.4.1 Spelling together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
Communication and collaboration: Writing skills as the learner writes 3-6 letter words correctly and clearly.

Values:
Responsibility: self-drive as the learner engages actively in word building activities with peers

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
Life skills: Effective communication as learner spells words correctly during signed dictation

Link to other Learning Areas

The learner is able to relate the skill of spelling words correctly to other learning areas such as Kiswahili and Environmental activities.

Suggested Learning Resources

Adapted course book, Chart, class readers, course books, flash cards, recording devices e.g tablets, mobile phone, dictionary, internet, signed audio- visual recordings
